document.title: Cable from Amembassy New Delhi to Secretary of State. "Subject: Letter from Gandhi to President Reagan on Narcotics, Afghanistan"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Text of Gandhi's February 26 letter on the U.S.-Indian narcotics working group and declining heroin production. It notes that disturbed conditions on the Afghan-Pakistan border are a major source of the problem and add to India's stake in an early Afghan settlement.

events.description: Reagan and Gandhi met in Washington and agreed the Indo-US Working Group on Narcotics should be convened early.
Indo-US Working Group on Narcotics met, with productive discussions on training and equipment.
Gandhi's letter to Reagan on narcotics and an early settlement in Afghanistan, delivered by Ronen Sen to the Ambassador.
Embassy New Delhi cabled the letter text to the Secretary of State.
Planned visit of Indian senior officials delegation to the US to study rehabilitation and welfare.
Gandhi and Reagan met in Washington and agreed to convene the Indo-US Working Group on Narcotics.
Indo-US Working Group on Narcotics met; productive discussions on training and equipment cooperation.
Gandhi wrote to Reagan on narcotics trends and the need for an early settlement in Afghanistan; Ronen Sen delivered it to the Ambassador that evening.
Embassy New Delhi cabled the letter text to the Secretary of State; Armacost to hand-carry the original to Washington.
Planned visit of Indian senior officials' delegation to the United States to study rehabilitation and welfare experience.
India–Pakistan discussions on narcotics; Pakistan agreed to exchange operational information.

relationships.quote: PRIME MINISTER GANDHI'S DIPLOMATIC ADVISER RONEN SEN DELIVERED LETTER

relationships.quote: DELIVERED LETTER REPRODUCED BELOW TO AMBASSADOR LATE EVENING OF FEBRUARY 26
DURING OUR MEETING IN WASHINGTON LAST OCTOBER, WE HAD AGREED

relationships.detail: Ronen Sen is Prime Minister Gandhi's diplomatic adviser.

relationships.quote: AMEMBASSY NEW DELHI TO SECSTATE WASHDC PRIORITY

relationships.detail: Gandhi is Prime Minister of India.
Reagan and Gandhi conducted a dialogue on drug trafficking and the need for an early settlement in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: LETTER DEALS WITH REAGAN/GANDHI DIALOGUE ON DRUG TRAFFICKING AND THE RELATED NEED FOR AN EARLY SETTLEMENT IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: India participates in the bilateral working group.
relationships.quote: THE INDO-US WORKING GROUP ON NARCOTICS SHOULD BE CONVENED AS EARLY AS POSSIBLE. THIS GROUP MET LAST MONTH

relationships.quote: AT A RECENT ROUND OF DISCUSSIONS WITH PAKISTAN, THEY AGREED TO OUR SUGGESTION FOR EXCHANGING OPERATIONAL INFORMATION

relationships.detail: India works on counter-drug cooperation within the SAARC framework.
relationships.quote: THROUGH BILATERAL CONTACTS AND WITHIN THE REGION'S FRAMEWORK OF SAARC

relationships.detail: The disturbed Afghan-Pakistan border is described as a major source of the drug problem.
relationships.quote: THE DISTURBED CONDITIONS ON THE AFGHAN-PAKISTAN BORDER IS ONE OF THE MAJOR SOURCES OF THE PROBLEM

relationships.detail: The border region lies partly in Pakistan.
relationships.quote: THE DISTURBED CONDITIONS ON THE AFGHAN-PAKISTAN BORDER

relationships.quote: RECENT INTERPOL ANALYSIS OF DRUG SEIZURES IN EUROPE SHOW A MARKED DECLINE IN THE PRODUCTION OF HEROIN OBTAINED FROM, OR THROUGH, INDIA

sources_cited: Interpol analysis of drug seizures in Europe
key_claims: Gandhi told Reagan Indian-linked heroin in European seizures fell from 52% in 1985 to 29% in 1986 and 8% in 1987.
India linked drug trafficking to the disturbed Afghan-Pakistan border and cited this as a reason for wanting an early Afghanistan settlement.
Pakistan agreed to exchange operational information on narcotics with India.
A large percentage of drugs seized by Indian agencies are of Pakistani origin.
